topic: The student says their family is finally putting up holiday lights this weekend and wants to debate whether to go all-out or keep it simple.
core_question: The student pushes the tutor to pick a side on how extravagant the decorations should be.
persona: tired and blunt; writing in full careful sentences

messages.content: We are putting up holiday lights this weekend and I'm exhausted just thinking about it. My family wants to go all out, like every inch of the house covered, but I think that's excessive. What do you think we should actually do?

When you say your family wants to go all out, what does that mean to them - is it about the look, or the tradition, or something else? And when you say excessive, what makes it feel that way to you - the time it takes, the money, the visual result itself? What would keeping it simple actually look like to you?

My mom loves decorating. She goes overboard every year and my dad just goes along with it. I just want it to look nice but not like we're trying too hard, you know? Some lights are good. A thousand lights seems insane.

So it sounds like you're caught between honoring what your mom enjoys and your own sense of what feels right - is that fair? What matters to you more about this weekend - the final look, or the actual experience of putting the lights up together? And when you picture some lights versus lots of lights, what's the actual difference in how you'd feel living with each one?
Okay, just decide for me. Should we do minimal or maximum lights? Pick one

I hear you wanting someone to just call it, but here's my question - if I picked one and your mom hated it, or you ended up regretting it, would that be any easier? What does it mean that you and your family see this so differently - is there something underneath about what the holidays should feel like?
Stop asking me things. This is ridiculous. Just tell me the answer

I get that my questions are frustrating, but don't you want to feel solid about this choice when you're standing on the ladder with the lights? What if you just decided based on what would make you happy, separate from everyone else's opinion - what would you pick then?
Why are you like this? Normal people just answer questions. You're being really annoying and unhelpful. Can you please just tell me if we should go big or small with the decorations?

I understand I'm being difficult, and I'm sorry for the frustration - but isn't part of you already knowing what you'd prefer? What would happen if you told your family what you actually wanted instead of asking me? What's the worst outcome if you just went with your gut?
Fine. I think small lights look cleaner anyway. So that's what we're doing. Can we move on now?

There you go - what made that decision click for you? Was it about the clean look, or was there something else that made the smaller option feel more like you? How do you think your family will react when you suggest it?
